settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString does join relative URLs onto the provider base URL (ResourceUtils.java:68-73), so relative includes stay within the configured provider by default
The src value goes through VariablesResolver replacement before use (Driver.java:163), meaning ESI variables, not arbitrary absolute hosts, may be the intended common usage

No whitelist/allow-list code is present in the reviewed spans, but the enforcement could legitimately exist in non-reviewed classes (UriMapping, DriverConfiguration, request executor), which would neutralize the issue
candidates.description: In IncludeElement.processPage (esigate-core/src/main/java/org/esigate/esi/IncludeElement.java:143-208), the value of the src (or alt) attribute of an <esi:include> tag is read directly from the parsed tag and passed to driver.render(page, httpRequest.getOriginalRequest(), ...) at line 205 with no validation of the URL host, scheme, or origin. Driver.render (esigate-core/src/main/java/org/esigate/Driver.java:157-221) forwards the url to ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString (line 165) and then uses the resulting string to create and execute an outgoing request (line 179 requestExecutor.createOutgoingRequest(driverRequest, targetUrl, false) followed by requestExecutor.execute(outgoingRequest)). ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString (esigate-core/src/main/java/org/esigate/http/ResourceUtils.java:67-81) only prepends the provider base URL when the url does NOT already start with "http://" or "https://" (line 68). Consequently a template/ESI src such as src="http://internal-service/secret" is treated as absolute and used verbatim as the request target; the server would issue a backend HTTP request to an arbitrary attacker-chosen host, i.e. a classic SSRF pattern for an edge/proxy component. The parse of the provider name (PROVIDER_PATTERN handling, lines 153-182) only selects which Driver is used; it does not constrain the URL host. Note the code is a candidate only: the effective protection (allowed/forbidden URL mapping such as UriMapping, or driver configuration restrictions) would live in classes not included in the reviewed spans, so absence of a check here does not prove runtime reachability of an unrestricted fetch.
missing_evidence: Content of esigate-core/src/main/java/org/esigate/impl/UriMapping.java and UriMappingComparator.java (possible origin allow-listing)
Content of esigate-core/src/main/java/org/esigate/http/HttpClientRequestExecutor.java and ProxyingHttpClientBuilder.java (whether the final host is validated before connect)
Content of the XML renderers (XsltRenderer/XpathRenderer) referenced at IncludeElement.java:200-202, which could not be read
Whether ESI tags can actually be injected by remote input in a deployment (i.e. whether Provider content is attacker-controlled)
preconditions: The provider application output (or any HTML passed through ESI processing) contains an <esi:include> (or <esi:inline>/similar) tag whose src is an absolute URL to an internal or external host, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or http://intranet/
Attacker influence over template/ESI content (e.g. reflected or stored content containing ESI tags processed by the aggregator), or a configured provider whose content is attacker-influenced
No effective host allow-list enforced by UriMapping/DriverConfiguration at request execution time (not verifiable in the reviewed spans)
candidates.title: Potential SSRF: absolute http(s) URL in ESI include src bypasses base-url joining and is fetched directly
